1. (Currently Amended) A golf tee comprising a long lasting combination of a golf tee and a force absorbing member in association therewith, said tee including a ground insertion end, a ball support end and a shaft in between, said member surrounding said shaft and being located below said ball support end and having an outer diameter less than that of a golf ball but large enough and located so as to protect said support end from impact from a golf club strike after a golf ball has been struck from said tee, wherein __the force absorbing member is fixedly attached to the shaft and is not slidable along the shaft__.

2. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 1, wherein said tee is formed from a material that enables the shaft to withstand damage from a strike on the resilient member __and wherein the force absorbing member comprises a material different from the material of the shaft__.

3. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 1, wherein said tee is formed from a member selected from the group consisting of wood, plastic and metal, __and wherein the force absorbing member is formed from a resilient elastomeric material__.

4. (Original) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from a hardwood.

5. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from an engineering plastic __and the force absorbing member is formed from neoprene__.

6. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 5, wherein said tee is formed from a polycarbonate __and the force absorbing member has a durometer hardness of from about 50 to about 60__.

7. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from nylon __and the force absorbing member is formed from neoprene__.

8. (Original) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from a malleable metal.

9. (Original) The golf tee of claim 8, wherein said tee is formed from aluminum.

10. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 9, wherein said force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising a natural or man-made material __and is fixedly attached to the shaft__.

11. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 1, wherein said force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising a natural or man-made material __and is fixedly attached to the shaft and not slidable along the shaft__.

12. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 11, wherein said force absorbing material has a hardness of from about 30 to about 90 durometer __and comprises neoprene__.

13. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 12, wherein said force absorbing material comprises a neoprene having a hardness of from about 50 to about 60 durometer __and is bonded to the shaft__.

14. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 11, wherein said force absorbing material comprises a neoprene __and is fixedly bonded to the shaft__.

15. (Currently Amended) A method of making a golf tee for use when striking a golf ball, said method comprising the step of forming a long lasting combination of a golf tee and a force absorbing member in association therewith, the tee including a ground insertion end, a ball support end and a shaft in between, wherein the member surrounding the shaft is located below the ball support end and has an outer diameter less than that of a golf ball but large enough and located so as to protect the support end from impact from a golf club strike after a golf ball has been struck from the tee, __and further comprising fixedly attaching the force absorbing member to the shaft such that it is not slidable along the shaft__.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 15, wherein the tee is formed from a material that enables the shaft to withstand damage from a strike on the resilient member __and wherein the force absorbing member comprises a material different from the material of the shaft__.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 15, wherein the tee is formed from a member selected from the group consisting of wood, plastic and metal, __and wherein the force absorbing member is formed from a resilient elastomeric material__.

18. (Original) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from a hardwood.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from an engineering plastic __and the force absorbing member is formed from neoprene__.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 19, wherein the tee is formed from a polycarbonate __and the force absorbing member has a durometer hardness of from about 50 to about 60__.

21. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from nylon __and the force absorbing member is formed from neoprene__.

22. (Original) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from a malleable metal.

23. (Original) The method of claim 22, wherein the tee is formed from aluminum.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 23, wherein the force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising a natural or man-made material __and is fixedly attached to the shaft__.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 15, wherein the force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising a natural or man-made material __and is fixedly attached to the shaft and not slidable along the shaft__.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the force absorbing material has a hardness of from about 30 to about 90 durometer __and comprises neoprene__.

27. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the force absorbing material comprises a neoprene having a hardness of from about 50 to about 60 durometer __and is bonded to the shaft__.

28. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the force absorbing material comprises a neoprene __and is fixedly bonded to the shaft__.
